newsitem.title: UK: NatWest retreats as bid fever cools.
newsitem.headline: NatWest retreats as bid fever cools.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc dropped on Tuesday, backtracking from their sharp gains of the past two sessions amid cautious press comment and as one brokerage trimmed earnings forecasts, dealers said.
NatWest shares were down 20p at 796 by 1040 GMT in active trade of over five million shares, putting it among the top ten active stocks in the London market at that point.
Analyst John Tyce at SocGen said he cut his top-of-the range 1997 pre-tax profit estimate for NatWest by 130 million stg to 1.9 billion and his 1998 forecast by 225 million stg to 2.275 billion.
Tyce said he maintained a "buy" recommendation on the stock but cautioned that it was hard to see much upside in the short-term.
He said NatWest appeared to have acknowledged its difficulties by its approach to Abbey National Plc and it would be no surprise if shareholders were unhappy with its recent underperformance.
"Possibly shareholders are getting more impatient than they used to be," Tyce said.

Separately a negative comment in the Financial Times Lex column encouraged profit-taking after NatWest's 80p rise in the past two sessions, driven by talk of a bid or merger involving the banking group, dealers said.

Dealers and analysts said on Monday there was talk that NatWest shareholders were unhappy about its share price underperformance of recent months and could put pressure on the bank to improve shareholder returns.

Yet Lex said NatWest shareholders "should steel themselves for further pain," adding that confirmation that NatWest had had talks with Abbey National Plc "is confirmation of the management's uncertainty about the outlook for organic growth".
Dealers said the Lex comment had helped undermine the stock. "Lex raised a certain amount of caution and profit-taking has definitely set in," said one.
Elsewhere in the bank sector, HSBC Holdings Plc was down 20p at 19.07-1/2, weighed down by a decline in shares in Hong Kong.
